Changes remain drafts (published:false), so no immediate runtime price change is claimed. Prevalidate the complete plan, patch affected axes transactionally under row/version fencing, and commit one audited outcome. Evidence: repro-ratio-apply-partial.log.

items.title: Global modal keyboard handlers can confirm a destructive action when Enter is pressed on Cancel and close a background drawer on Escape

Scope Enter handling to the text input/form and let native Cancel/Confirm button semantics apply; centralize top-layer Escape, IME handling, focus restoration and scroll lock in a modal lifecycle component. items.validation: Actual ChannelDrawer built outside the repository and exercised in isolated headless Chromium. Typing seed into an injected-field name yields only s and focus is lost; typing test into a custom-header name yields only t and focus is lost. These row keys include the edited name, so the row remounts every keystroke. No real API writes. Use stable row identities and a shared key-value editor whose draft survives key edits. Evidence: repro-channel-form.log.

items.title: Editing a disabled or date-scoped pricing rule silently enables it and erases its validity window
items.validation: Actual RuleDrawer in isolated headless Chromium: initial enabled=false and validity 2099-01-01..2099-02-01, Save payload omits enabled/valid_from/valid_to. Replayed that exact payload (only rule_code changed to synthetic unique code) through the real console router against isolated PG/Redis: HTTP 200, stored enabled=true and both validity bounds NULL. Draft pricing only; publication remains required, so this is not immediate live-price mutation. Full-replacement vs partial-update contract must be explicit; preserve unedited lifecycle fields or use a typed patch. Evidence: repro-rule-ui.log and repro-rule-lifecycle.log.

items.title: A late refund lookup can show bill A in confirmation while submitting mutable input bill B
items.validation: Actual RefundCard in isolated Chromium, all requests intercepted. Start lookup for valid UUID A, edit input to valid UUID B before response, then release A response. Preview/confirmation shows User A and USD1.00, but outgoing refund POST contains request_id B. No real refund/financial changes. Use lookup variables/operation identity, ignore responses for stale drafts, and submit the immutable preview request_id captured at confirmation. Evidence: repro-refund-preview.log.

items.title: Portal cache trend ignores observation coverage and turns unknown cache rates into zero or diluted percentages
items.validation: Ran the actual TypeScript usageChart/cacheHit functions via the installed TypeScript transpiler outside the repo. Identical unobserved cache data: KPI {bp:null,samples:0}, trend value 0. Partial sample: measured 50 cache / 100 observed prompt with 200 total prompt gives KPI 50% (partial 1/2 requests), trend 25% without coverage distinction. Centralize coverage-aware rate aggregation; render unknown gaps and label paired partial samples. No API writes. Evidence: repro-cache-chart.log.

items.title: Default E2E server reuse can mutate the running demo database and overwrite its site notice
items.validation: Source-confirmed conditional test-environment defect; not executed against any business server. The default config uses console port 8081 and reuseExistingServer=true. Non-mocked smoke tests log in with the demo admin, POST a site_notice, then overwrite it with a disabled empty notice instead of restoring the prior value. They also register users/create keys; screenshots opt-in additionally mutate settings/health. If the running server contains the demo admin, a normal E2E run can change its shared data. Use a mandatory disposable environment and separate fully mocked from real-API suites; original state restoration alone does not make shared integration tests isolated.

items.title: Rust integration fixtures load the developer database and overwrite global security/payment/mail settings without restoring them
items.validation: Source-confirmed conditional test-environment risk, not run against any business database. Default dotenv DATABASE_URL/OKAPI_REDIS_URL are accepted without a disposable-environment check. OAuth fixtures set shared ssrf_policy allow_http=true/allow_private=true; subscription fixtures replace payment_epay; SMTP fixtures replace smtp/notify_channels then delete smtp without restoring its prior value and leave notify_channels. UUID users/models do not isolate global settings or worker queue scans. Retention/image-batch fixtures already use their own temporary databases and are positive examples, not affected by the global retention-drop allegation. Enforce per-suite disposable PG and Redis namespace and unique CH/NATS resources; restore injections on failure via scoped lifecycle. CH 24.8 serial full run additionally failed request_population only at the unscoped site total (13 != 1): preceding own-user populations, refund, token and raw-event assertions passed. Its mirror helper drains the shared PG outbox into its private CH database; not evidence of double charging. The same test passed in a newly created PostgreSQL database and Redis DB 4 on ClickHouse 24.8 (1 passed, exit 0), supporting shared fixture-state contamination rather than refund double-counting. See request-population-fresh.log.
